readings: For each player in the postseason batting data (matched to `player` on `player_id`), take their average postseason doubles per record, ignoring missing values, along with their batting hand. Divide it by the overall average of these per-player averages to get a relative index. Then show how far each player's index sits above the average index for their batting hand. Give the top 10 players by that gap, largest first (missing last), with player id, batting hand, average doubles, index, and the gap, unrounded.
queries:
WITH player_averages AS (
    SELECT
        p.player_id,
        p.bats,
        AVG(bp.double) AS avg_doubles
    FROM batting_postseason AS bp
    JOIN player AS p ON p.player_id = bp.player_id
    GROUP BY p.player_id, p.bats
),
player_indices AS (
    SELECT
        player_id,
        bats,
        avg_doubles,
        avg_doubles / NULLIF((SELECT AVG(avg_doubles) FROM player_averages), 0) AS relative_index
    FROM player_averages
),
player_gaps AS (
    SELECT
        player_id,
        bats,
        avg_doubles,
        relative_index,
        relative_index - AVG(relative_index) OVER (PARTITION BY bats) AS gap
    FROM player_indices
)
SELECT player_id, bats, avg_doubles, relative_index, gap
FROM player_gaps
ORDER BY gap IS NULL, gap DESC
LIMIT 10;
